# Kimi K3 — Round 3 (final)

**Framing check.** The matrix represents me correctly — including where it corrects me. O1 fact (i) stands: the full monthly score (+36.83 vs 32.23) was published 2026-08-09, so my "literal reading first computed 2026-10-15" was wrong for panel a. Conceded. What survives: the gate fixed *before the run* was the thinned one (fact ii — my own blueprint-round reservation), and the literal comparison remains unpaired, across different origin sets and base rates, +2.19 against a 2.99 block margin.

**N1 — acceptable.** Oracle-free leads, triple print, power clause inline. I drop fixed-λ-first for a reason beyond live-availability: the key's preregistered scoring reference is +20.4, and the headline and the number we are judged against should be the same number. Condition: labels exact — nested +18.32 is oracle-censored, printed as an upper bound for nested-oracle-free.

**N2 — yes, I can live without 4.42.** The draft as written is strictly better than my two tiers: the own-critical-value tier already does the agenda work, and 4.42 fires at 0.41 SE (4.42/(21.06/1.96)) — noise. One-sided Δ on common origins, 1.96·SD_block recomputed each refit, renamed critical value, 80%-power MDE and leave-one-block-out and three-start Δ printed beside. Adopt as drafted.

**N3 — accept Claude's formula.** L_R = max(18, max lag_peak, max lag_trough − 12) = max(18, 12, 9) = 18 today. It is my two-parameter rule collapsed into one sufficient statistic: the −12 is the label window, and a trough lag must exceed 30 months to flip a matured row. Write my eligibility condition (age ≥ L_R AND censoring status resolved with information at R) as the rule's sentence; audit both lags annually. **I would not sign L_R = 21**: a permanent 3-month tax on every origin, and on positive-label entry under the content trigger, against a mechanism that has never bound — chosen after seeing it costs N = 271 → 270. Evidence that changes my mind: a historical trough lag > 30, or one demonstrated censored→0 flip of a matured origin.

**O1 — final: quarterly.** The only paired evidence (three thinnings) puts the quarter-end phase *worse* than quarterly (26.03 vs 27.05); Fable's covariate-count point is real for the fit, but the measured effect is β −1.29 → −1.41 and P 14.9 → 14.4 — reweighting the same episodes, not new cycles. Compromise: **(b)** — quarterly retained; minutes state the §2 literal gate passed and the council overrode it, with reasons; monthly-fit P logged unscored from 2027; spec-governs-code prospectively, both directions. I can live with (a) only under four conditions: sealed λ-normalisation (summed vs averaged loss) pushed before any monthly run; permanent parallel quarterly publication; the two scores never printed as comparable or as an improvement; spec-governs-code adopted generally. **VETO: monthly adoption without the sealed normalisation** — under a summed loss, λ = 1 on ~800 rows is a different penalty than on 267; that is a model change smuggled in as a frequency change. Evidence that flips me: a paired common-origin comparison with monthly ahead beyond its block margin; E2 contains nothing resembling it.

**O2 — final: adopt.** Claude's one-refit-per-onset is strictly better than the 18-in-49 version — same dating correction at a third of the churn. I take it, with Sol/DeepSeek's sealed configuration-specific replay published as the ledger supplement. Fallback if Fable/Grok hold out: September + hash is tolerable (max ΔP 1.05 pp); no veto from me either direction.

**O3 — accept the candidate text verbatim.** Historical sealed test closed permanently (the onset pattern has been seen; snapshots audit revisions, not contamination); EBP stays a context line; any future evaluation is prospective-only, sealed before any onset it would be judged on, with no pre-2027 data as evidence. No veto.

**Vetoes restated:** monthly fit without sealed λ-normalisation; L_R = 21. Everything else above is signable.
